sentences.text: Amylodon is an extinct genus of chimaera that includes four described species.
Scientists know these animals mainly from isolated mandibles, which are lower jaws.
The species A. karamysh was named after the Karamysh River near its type locality in Russia.
Species of Amylodon show a gradual progression toward increased shearing ability.
The parent group of Amylodon is the family Rhinochimaeridae.
While some studies classified Amylodon in Chimaeridae, others assigned it to Edaphodontidae or Rhinochimaeridae.
This genus lived from the Campanian to the Lutetian, spanning between 83.6 and 41.03 million years ago.
One species, A. karamysh, inhabited Russia during the latest early Campanian.
Other species, A. venablesae and A. eocenica, lived in England during the Ypresian age.
